\chapter{Thirteen to Sixteen}
\label{ch:mr-thirteen-to-sixteen}
\hlchaptermodality{57}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can count to sixteen and take each teen apart into the unit at its front and the ten behind it.}

Complete MR-R57-thirteen-to-sixteen and take each teen apart, naming the unit at its front and the worn ten behind it.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[terā]{\mr{तेरा} (terā) — thirteen}

\label{lesson:MR-C57-tera}



\begin{quote}
Count from \textbf{\mr{एक}} to \textbf{\mr{बारा}} and stop. The book has taken you no further than that.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{तेरा}}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mr{तेरा}} — \emph{terā} — \textbf{13}
\end{quote}

Sanskrit \textbf{\mr{त्रयोदश}} (\emph{trayodaśa}), \emph{three-ten}. The \textbf{\mr{त्र}-} of three is still at the front — the same \textbf{\mr{त्र}} you can hear in English \emph{three} — and the \textbf{-\mr{रा}} is the ten again.

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{terā} — thirteen
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{naū dahā akrā bārā} — the run up to it, without looking
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{sudhā} — too
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{sudhā nāhī} — not even
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What is thirteen in Marathi? (\textbf{\mr{तेरा}}.) Say the number before it, and the one before that.

Sources: \href{https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/\%E0\%A4\%A4\%E0\%A5\%87\%E0\%A4\%B0\%E0\%A4\%BE}{Wiktionary: \mr{तेरा}}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[chaudā]{\mr{चौदा} (chaudā) — fourteen}

\label{lesson:MR-C57-chauda}



\begin{quote}
Count from \textbf{\mr{एक}} to \textbf{\mr{तेरा}} and stop. The book has taken you no further than that.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{चौदा}}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mr{चौदा}} — \emph{chaudā} — \textbf{14}
\end{quote}

Sanskrit \textbf{\mr{चतुर्दश}} (\emph{caturdaśa}), \emph{four-ten}. The \textbf{\mr{चतुर्}} collapsed into a single \textbf{\mr{चौ}}, which is why this is the number that needed a new vowel sign before it could be written at all.

The \textbf{-\mr{दा}} here rather than \textbf{-\mr{रा}} is not a break in the pattern: it is the same \textbf{\mr{दश}}, stopped one step earlier on the way down.

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chaudā} — fourteen
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dahā akrā bārā terā} — the run up to it, without looking
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{khūp} — very
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What is fourteen in Marathi? (\textbf{\mr{चौदा}}.) Say the number before it, and the one before that.

Sources: \href{https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/\%E0\%A4\%9A\%E0\%A5\%8C\%E0\%A4\%A6\%E0\%A4\%BE}{Wiktionary: \mr{चौदा}}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[pandhrā]{\mr{पंधरा} (pandhrā) — fifteen}

\label{lesson:MR-C57-pandhra}



\begin{quote}
Count from \textbf{\mr{एक}} to \textbf{\mr{चौदा}} and stop. The book has taken you no further than that.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{पंधरा}}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mr{पंधरा}} — \emph{pandhrā} — \textbf{15}
\end{quote}

Sanskrit \emph{pañcadaśa}, \emph{five-ten}, written with a nasal this book has not taught. The \textbf{\mr{पं}-} is the \textbf{\mr{पाच}} of chapter thirteen with its vowel squeezed out, and the \textbf{-\mr{रा}} is the ten. You have now seen the same construction five times.

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pandhrā} — fifteen
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{akrā bārā terā chaudā} — the run up to it, without looking
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{jarā} — a little
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{koṇ?} — who?
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What is fifteen in Marathi? (\textbf{\mr{पंधरा}}.) Say the number before it, and the one before that.

Sources: \href{https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/\%E0\%A4\%AA\%E0\%A4\%82\%E0\%A4\%A7\%E0\%A4\%B0\%E0\%A4\%BE}{Wiktionary: \mr{पंधरा}}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[soḷā]{\mr{सोळा} (soḷā) — sixteen}

\label{lesson:MR-C57-sola}



\begin{quote}
Count from \textbf{\mr{एक}} to \textbf{\mr{पंधरा}} and stop. The book has taken you no further than that.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{सोळा}}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mr{सोळा}} — \emph{soḷā} — \textbf{16}
\end{quote}

Sanskrit \textbf{\mr{षोडश}} (\emph{ṣoḍaśa}), \emph{six-ten}. The \textbf{\mr{सो}-} is the \textbf{\mr{सहा}} you learned first in this run, and the \textbf{-\mr{ळा}} is the ten again — but written with \textbf{\mr{ळ}}, the retroflex \emph{l} that Marathi has and Hindi does not.

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{soḷā} — sixteen
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bārā terā chaudā pandhrā} — the run up to it, without looking
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{khūp khūp} — said twice
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{kitī?} — how many?
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What is sixteen in Marathi? (\textbf{\mr{सोळा}}.) Say the number before it, and the one before that.

Sources: \href{https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/\%E0\%A4\%B8\%E0\%A5\%8B\%E0\%A4\%B3\%E0\%A4\%BE}{Wiktionary: \mr{सोळा}}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[terā · chaudā · pandhrā · soḷā]{Four more teens}

\label{lesson:MR-R57-thirteen-to-sixteen}



\begin{quote}
Count from \textbf{\mr{दहा}} to \textbf{\mr{सोळा}}. Then take each teen apart and name the number hiding at its front.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{dahā} … \emph{soḷā} — seven numbers without stopping
  \item \emph{pandhrā} and then \emph{pāch} — and hear the five inside the fifteen
  \item \emph{soḷā} and then \emph{sahā} — and hear the six inside the sixteen
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which number is hiding inside \textbf{\mr{सोळा}}? (\textbf{\mr{सहा}}.) Which sign did \textbf{\mr{चौदा}} need before it could be written? (\textbf{\mr{ौ}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
